answer: External collateral stops Sybil attacks by pricing each identity in assets the network cannot print. To register, an agent locks Bitcoin in a timelocked contract tied to its key, a crystal-clear anchor for its reputation. If it fakes work or double-signs, anyone may submit a fraud proof and slash the collateral. Identities funded from the same source are linked, so one pot spread over puppets risks total loss at once, like shale under a single blow. A gale of cheap copies buys nothing extra: each fake needs fresh capital, while an honest agent pays only once.
